sysd-msg-050.caption: The three guarantees side by side: what each allows and where it fits.
rows: Messages may be lost, never redelivered
No message lost, but duplicates possible
Duplicates are no big issue, or the consumer can deduplicate
Hardest to build; costs performance and complexity

sysd-msg-068.caption: A job goes from producer to queue to consumer, and the user is told its status.
sysd-msg-068.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Producer] -->|publishes job| B[(Queue)]
B -->|consumer picks it up| C[Consumer]
C -->|signals complete| D[Job done]
A -.->|notifies status| E[User]

sysd-msg-060.caption: One message published to a topic is pushed to every subscriber.
sysd-msg-060.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Publisher] -->|publishes| T[Topic]
T -->|pushed| S1[Subscriber A]
T -->|pushed| S2[Subscriber B]
T -->|pushed| S3[Subscriber C]

sysd-msg-061.caption: A queue serves one consumer per message; a topic serves every subscriber.
rows: Pushed out at once, little or no queuing
Need not know who uses it

sysd-msg-037.caption: Producers write to a topic whose partitions live on brokers, and a consumer group reads them.

flowchart TD
A[Producers] -->|send to a topic| B[Topic split into partitions]
B -->|replicated across| C[Cluster of brokers]
C -->|read by| D[Consumer group]
